sbe:messageSchema.description: Node-local replay control protocol between a ReplayerService and its co-located app replicas

sbe:message.name: ReplayRequest
sbe:message.description: A replica asks its Replayer to replay the sequenced stream. Either it is cold-starting and walks the full recording chain by segmentIndex, or it detected a globalSeqNo gap and resumes the active recording at fromPosition

field.name: clientId
field.description: Requesting replica's stable id, unique among the Replayer's co-located apps

field.name: requestId
field.description: Monotone per-client request counter, incremented on every send INCLUDING a verbatim resend, and echoed in the Replaying/ReplayPending that answers it. The app ignores any reply whose requestId is not its current one: a resend makes the Replayer supersede the in-flight replay and start a new one, so the stale reply for the stopped session is still queued ahead of the live one on the shared control stream, and acting on it would attach to (or wait for) a replay session that no longer exists

field.name: fromPosition
field.description: Recording position to resume the active recording from (SequencedEvent.position of the last in-order frame); used only when segmentIndex < 0

field.name: segmentIndex
field.description: -1 = resume the current active recording at fromPosition (steady-state gap). >=0 = cold-start walk: replay the segmentIndex-th recording of the sequenced stream's per-leader-tenure chain (oldest first) from position 0. The app walks 0,1,2,… de-duping by globalSeqNo (contiguous across tenures) until the Replayer answers NO_REPLAY_NEEDED, which marks it caught up. This spans every failover, so a cold start after a leader change recovers full history

sbe:message.name: Replaying
sbe:message.description: The Replayer started an archive replay for the requesting replica; the app attaches to replaySessionId on the Replayer replay stream and follows it until its image position reaches catchUpPosition, then falls back to the live tap (de-duped by globalSeqNo)

field.name: requestId
field.description: Echo of the answered ReplayRequest.requestId; the app ignores a reply that is not for its current request

field.name: replaySessionId
field.description: Aeron replay session id to attach to (Subscription.imageBySessionId) on the Replayer replay stream

field.name: catchUpPosition
field.description: Recording position the bounded replay ends at; the app is caught up once its replay image reaches this and switches to the live tap. A bounded replay of an active recording does not close its image at the bound, so completion is detected by position (as ClusterStreamClient does for its live segment), not by image close

field.name: recordingId
field.description: Archive recordingId the reply was served from; -1 when replaySessionId is NO_REPLAY_NEEDED because the walk ran past the end of the chain (no specific recording to name). That -1 is what terminates a cold-start walk: a NO_REPLAY_NEEDED that still names a recording means only that THAT segment is empty, and the app skips it and requests the next one rather than declaring the chain exhausted. serveReplay re-resolves the recording chain on every request (ReplayerService.resolveSegments), and ReplayRecordings.stitch can drop a stale still-recording span once a newer one supersedes it — shifting which recording a given segmentIndex denotes. The app remembers the recordingId it last saw for its current segmentIndex and compares on every reply for that same index: a mismatch means the chain moved under it, so it abandons the walk and restarts from segment 0 rather than risk replaying the wrong span

sbe:message.name: ReplayPending
sbe:message.description: The Replayer has >=2 replays already active; the requesting replica must hold at its gap (must not advance past the hole) until a later Replaying arrives

field.name: requestId
field.description: Echo of the answered ReplayRequest.requestId; the app ignores a reply that is not for its current request

sbe:message.name: ReplayComplete
sbe:message.description: A replica has finished with its replay (caught up to the tip and switched to the live tap) and no longer needs its slot; the Replayer frees it immediately (design §5) rather than waiting for the idle-TTL, and hands it to any waiting app. Sent after a steady-state gap resume; a cold-start walk needs none, since each of its slots is freed by the supersede on the next segment request

sbe:message.name: ReplayHeartbeat
sbe:message.description: Sent by a replica every ~500ms for as long as it is running an attached replay image, and refreshes that client's slot. This is what makes the slot TTL an IDLE timeout rather than a max lifetime: a replay has no upper time bound (the design mandates full-log replay, and the log grows all trading day), so a slot aged only from when it was activated is reclaimed mid-flight on any replay that outlives the TTL — stopping the replay under a healthy client. A client that died or wedged stops heart-beating and is still reclaimed on schedule

sbe:message.name: ReplayUnavailable
sbe:message.description: The Replayer's startup integrity check failed — this node's oldest tap recording does not reach globalSeqNo 1 (deleted, corrupted, or a partial restore), so it has no valid history to serve any replica. Distinct from ReplayPending, which means 'hold, a slot will free': this is permanent for the Replayer's lifetime. Refusing here is what keeps a broken archive contained to the Replayer — served anyway, the replay's first frame would not be globalSeqNo 1 and every co-located app would independently abort on its own baseline check

field.name: requestId
field.description: Echo of the refused ReplayRequest.requestId; the app ignores a reply that is not for its current request
